messages:
anya: quick sync: legal + sales asked us to define how regional egress caps interact with per-route throughput add-ons. customers are confused when they buy a throughput add-on but hit region egress limits. need a clear product stance.

jose: Problem: add-ons currently increase route token/min but egress caps are enforced per-region per-account. so you can buy bandwidth but still get throttled by regional cap. not good.

priya: Sales reports a churn risk with enterprise customers launching global rollouts. They expect add-ons to either bypass regional caps or adjust them automatically.

samir: From infra POV we can't let add-ons silently bypass hard regional capacity — that defeats capacity planning. Options: (A) surface preflight check that shows effective limits (route + region) before purchase; (B) make add-on purchase optionally include a matching region cap uplift SKU; (C) auto-provision temporary region uplift for X hours after purchase with approvals.

anya: I prefer explicit behavior so customers aren't surprised. lean to B + A: require customers to either buy a region uplift SKU or see a warning that their existing regional cap will still apply.

sylvia: Accounting/legal prefers discrete SKUs to track revenue and avoid hidden commitments. Clause draft: "Add-on throughput increases route-level limits; regional capacity limits remain enforced unless a region-cap SKU or reserved capacity contract is purchased."

jose: UI idea: during add-on checkout, show an "Effective Limits" panel: tokens/min by-route, region remaining headroom, and suggested region SKUs if headroom insufficient. maybe a small calculation: effective = min(route_limit + addon, region_remaining).

priya: Sales wants an auto-recommendation flow: if customer chooses global add-on, recommend per-region uplift SKUs with estimated cost. Also want a partner-facing variant for partner-enabled accounts.

samir: Implementation notes: backend must compute region_remaining at time of purchase (need eventual-consistent caches) and create a cart flow for region SKUs. If we offer temporary auto-provision, we must add approval guardrails and TTLs.

ops-bot: feature-flag proposal: "region-aware-addon-checkout". canary ready for experiment.

anya: Launch criteria proposal: 1) Checkout flow shows Effective Limits and recommended SKUs; 2) Billing can create region-cap SKU orders; 3) Legal approved wording; 4) Telemetry: <2% support tickets about unexpected throttling in pilot; 5) Partner flow tested.

sylvia: I'll draft the invoice line samples and the contract snippet: include clear auto-expiry and a note that reserved capacity SKUs carry a minimum-term.

jose: Tech tasks: API to compute region_remaining (cheap read path), UI panel + recommendation engine, and a new SKU type region_cap_{region}_{units}. Also add a warning banner when effective < requested.

priya: Pilot plan: roll out to 10 customers in EU and APAC who asked for multi-region launches. Sales will run the recommendation flow and track conversion.

samir: Ops guard: if region_remaining calculation is stale we should show conservative estimate and block checkout with a "contact support" CTA. Also emit metric: checkout_recommendation_conversion and support_ticket_rate.

anya: Decision recap: do not silently bypass region caps. Implement region-aware add-on checkout that computes effective limits, recommends region-cap SKUs, and allows customers to purchase region uplifts as discrete SKUs. Default UX shows warnings. Action items: Jose - api + recommendation logic; Samir - stale data guard + ops hooks; Sylvia - invoice + contract language; Priya - pilot customers + sales templates; Anya - update PRD and launch checklist.

jose: noted. will open PR for region_remaining API this afternoon.

sylvia: drafting clause and SKU naming conventions, will post to #legal.

priya: lining up pilot customers; will share scripts for sales demos.

anya: great. sync back after pilot conversion numbers and support ticket review. :white_check_mark:
